description: We are a passionate and collaborative team interested in technology, space science, AI and solving real-world problems with innovative ideas. Our team has experience in software development, AI/ML, data analysis, research and web/mobile application development.
summary:
What we developed: We developed AstraVital AI, an autonomous astronaut health intelligence and 3D physiological digital twin platform designed for long-duration deep space missions, including the Artemis Moon base and crewed Mars expeditions.

How it addresses the challenge: AstraVital AI bridges real-time biosensor telemetry with authentic spaceflight biology research from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), GeneLab, and NTRS clinical standards (NASA-STD-3001). The system continuously tracks ten core physiological parameters, synchronizes vitals with an interactive 3D humanoid digital twin to visualize microgravity organ stress (such as SANS, cardiac remodeling, and bone demineralization), and utilizes an explainable clinical decision-support engine.

Why it is important: Deep space missions face communication delays of up to 22 minutes each way, making real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible. By delivering autonomous anomaly detection, predictive risk forecasting, and radiation shelter triage directly aboard spacecraft, AstraVital AI protects astronaut health and mission success when Earth is out of reach.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

AstraVital AI is an autonomous astronaut health intelligence and 3D physiological digital twin platform designed for long-duration deep space exploration (Artemis Lunar Base and crewed Mars missions). It operates through an integrated full-stack architecture comprising eight core subsystems:

  • Live Telemetry & Biosensor Engine: Continuously streams and monitors ten critical physiological parameters (Heart Rate, Blood Oxygen (SpO₂), Core Body Temperature, Blood Pressure, Respiration Rate, Sleep Duration, Physical Exercise Counters, Autonomic Stress Score, Ionizing Radiation Dosimetry, and Intravascular Hydration).
  • 3D Astronaut Digital Twin: A WebGL/Three.js anatomical model that dynamically synchronizes in real time with astronaut telemetry, visually mapping organ-level microgravity strain across the left ventricle, brain/optic nerve (SANS), axial spine, and femur.
  • Astra AI Clinical Decision Support: An edge-deployable clinical inference engine that detects physiological anomalies, projects risk trajectories, and provides explainable, multi-factor medical recommendations based on NASA clinical practice guidelines.
  • NASA Research Explorer & Library: Directly connects real-time telemetry to authentic spaceflight biology studies from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), GeneLab, and the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS).
  • Autonomous Crew Interfaces: Includes an interactive Space Weather Hub querying the NASA DONKI API for real-time solar flare and radiation warnings, a Mental Wellness Center running Psychomotor Vigilance Tasks (PVT-B), and a Mars Mission Simulator modeling physiological degradation over 30 to 1,000 days of interplanetary transit.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero-Latency Clinical Autonomy: Solves the critical communication delay between Earth and deep space by providing onboard, instant medical triage without waiting for Houston flight surgeons.
  • Holistic Physiological & Environmental Fusion: Combines internal biosignals (ECG waveforms, hemodynamics) with external space environment factors (solar particle events, ambient cabin radiation).
  • Transparent Scientific Grounding: Establishes clear data provenance by distinguishing authentic NASA peer-reviewed data from simulated telemetry, giving flight crews and flight surgeons transparent citations for every clinical recommendation.
  • Proactive Countermeasure Optimization: Dynamically adjusts exercise regimens on the Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) and calculates radiation shelter protocols before irreversible bone resorption or radiation sickness occurs.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

As humanity expands beyond Low Earth Orbit toward the Moon and Mars, medical emergencies cannot be treated with terrestrial hospital evacuation or real-time telemedicine. AstraVital AI serves as an indispensable digital chief medical officer aboard exploration spacecraft.

Its long-term impact extends beyond spaceflight: the platform’s edge architecture, lightweight sensor integration, and explainable decision algorithms can be directly adapted for terrestrial telemedicine in remote, isolated, and austere environments—including Antarctic research outposts, rural clinical clinics, and disaster response zones.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3 (Modern Glassmorphic UI design).
    • Three.js & WebGL: For the real-time 3D Astronaut Digital Twin and celestial orbital mechanics (ISS Earth & Mars transit).
    • Chart.js: For high-frequency, multi-parameter real-time biosensor telemetry streaming.
    • HTML5 Canvas API: For rendering a 60 fps continuous ECG Lead II cardiac waveform.
    • Web Speech API & Web Audio API: For voice synthesis and hands-free microphone input.
  • Backend & Server Architecture: Node.js, Express.js REST API, and Server-Sent Events (SSE) for persistent live telemetry streaming.
  • Data Sources & APIs: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), NASA GeneLab, NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), NASA DONKI API (api.nasa.gov), and NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center.
  • Mobile & Packaging Software: Progressive Web App (PWA Service Worker), Capacitor, Android SDK, and Gradle for building native Android APKs (AstraVital-AI.apk).
  • Deployment & Cloud: Vercel cloud hosting and Git version control.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Anatomical Stress Mapping via 3D Digital Twin: Rather than displaying isolated numbers on a spreadsheet, AstraVital AI translates complex telemetry into an intuitive, glowing 3D anatomical heat map that instantly shows flight crews which organs (e.g., optic nerve edema from cephalad fluid shift) are undergoing acute microgravity strain.
  • Research-to-Dashboard Context Engine: Clicking any anomalous vital parameter immediately surfaces the underlying biological mechanism and the exact NASA OSDR multi-omics study or NTRS paper explaining why microgravity caused that shift.
  • Hands-Free Operational Modality: Astronauts during intravehicular (IVA) maintenance or suited operations cannot use keyboards; AstraVital AI incorporates hands-free voice synthesis and voice command recognition.
  • Multi-Scenario Simulation Sandbox: Includes a deterministic seed-based scenario injector allowing flight surgeons and crew to rehearse Nominal, Autonomic Stress, and Solar Particle Event (SPE) emergency scenarios.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Communication Latency: Designed entirely around the reality of light-speed delays (up to 22 minutes one-way to Mars), mandating local, client-side/edge computational autonomy.
  • Strict Scientific Provenance & Ethics: Transparently enforced a strict three-tier classification taxonomy (Real Research Data, Simulated Telemetry, and Derived Analytics) to ensure judges, researchers, and crew never confuse synthetic sensor demonstration with actual astronaut clinical records.
  • Spaceflight Human-System Standards: Calibrated all nominal thresholds and alert triggers against NASA-STD-3001 (Crew Health & Habitability Standards) and NASA clinical practice guidelines.
  • Cognitive Load & Crew Usability: In high-stress orbital environments, information overload can be fatal. We designed high-contrast glassmorphic visuals, one-click triage views, and a dedicated Mission Control multi-astronaut overview display to enable split-second decision-making.
